bounties.title: Listen to Voice Clips and Label Emotions
bounties.description:
Take part in a listening study that takes about 45 minutes. Listen to English voice clips and choose the emotion and speaking-style labels that best describe each voice.

Please use headphones or work somewhere quiet, listen to every clip fully, and answer carefully.

You will receive $10 for completing the study, plus a $0.50 attention bonus if your labels match our expert labels, for careful completion and following the labeling instructions. Two practice rounds with expert feedback will show you how the task works.

After finishing the study, you must return to this task page, upload the completion code as evidence, and mark the task as complete. Both steps are required so we can review your submission and issue payment.
requirements: Comfortable understanding spoken English
Use headphones or a quiet environment
Complete the study only once
Listen fully and answer honestly
Desktop or laptop recommended
After finishing, upload the completion code as evidence and mark the task as complete on this platform
bounties.completionCriteria: Complete the entire listening study, follow the audio and labeling instructions, upload the unique completion code shown on the final screen as evidence on this task page, and mark the task as complete. One completed submission per participant.
bounties.evidenceCriteria: Upload the unique completion code displayed on the study's final screen as evidence on this task page and mark the task as complete.

bounties.title: Data Annotation Test Task (Text, Image & Audio) — Only US and Long-Term Opportunity
bounties.description:
We are looking for a skilled data annotator based in the United States to complete a test annotation task across three data types. Successfully completing this test assignment could lead to long-term collaboration and ongoing paid work.

**Task Breakdown:**
- **Text Annotation:** Sentiment labeling for 15 text snippets (positive, negative, neutral)
- **Image Annotation:** Bounding box annotation for 23 images
- **Audio Annotation:** Transcription for 7 audio clips

**Instructions:**
- All annotations must be accurate, consistent, and follow the provided guidelines (shared upon acceptance).
- Work must be completed carefully and submitted in the required format.
- Only US citizens are eligible to apply.

**Why Apply?**
This is a test task designed to evaluate your skills and attention to detail. High-quality performers will be considered for a long-term annotation contract with regular, ongoing assignments.
requirements: Must be a US citizen
Must be based in the United States
Experience with data annotation (text, image, or audio)
Attention to detail and consistency
Ability to follow annotation guidelines and deliver in the required format
bounties.completionCriteria: All 15 text snippets are labeled with sentiment (positive, negative, or neutral). All 23 images have accurate bounding boxes drawn around the specified objects. All 7 audio clips are fully transcribed. Annotations are submitted in the required format with no missing items.
bounties.evidenceCriteria: Include a brief text summary confirming completion of each category (15 text snippets, 23 images, 7 audio clips).

bounties.title: Mascot / Character Costume Performer – SEO Conference, Brighton (Oct 8–9)
bounties.description:
We are exhibiting at an SEO Conference in Brighton, UK, and are looking for an enthusiastic, professional character costume performer to wear our company mascot costume for two full days.

**Event Details:**
- Dates: Thursday 8 October & Friday 9 October 2026
- Hours: 8:45 AM – 4:45 PM each day (~8 hours/day)
- Location: Brighton, UK (full venue address shared upon confirmation)

**Role Overview:**
You will wear our company-provided mascot costume and represent our brand at our exhibition booth and occasionally outside the venue. Your role includes waving to visitors, posing for photos, and creating a fun, welcoming atmosphere at our stand. This is a corporate, professional environment — an SEO industry conference — so friendly, enthusiastic, and composed behaviour is essential.

**Important details:**
- The costume is fully provided by us — you do not need to source anything.
- All movement between the booth and outdoors will be chaperoned by a member of our exhibition staff at all times. You will never be left to navigate the venue alone.
- The on-site contact person's details will be shared with you once confirmed.
- The role is not physically strenuous — primarily standing, waving, and posing for photos.
- We strongly prefer the same performer for both days to keep communication simple, please note your availability clearly.

**Ideal Candidate:**
- Height: approximately 5'5"–5'6"
- Build: on the smaller side (important for costume fit)
- Friendly, confident, and comfortable being in a costume in a public corporate setting
- Punctual and professional
requirements: Must be available both Thursday 8 October and Friday 9 October 2026, 8:45 AM – 4:45 PM
Ideal height: 5'5"–5'6"
Smaller build preferred for costume fit
Comfortable wearing a full character costume in a corporate public setting
Professional, friendly, and punctual
Must be based in or able to travel to Brighton, UK
bounties.completionCriteria: The performer has attended both full days (8 October and 9 October 2026) from 8:45 AM to approximately 4:45 PM, worn the provided mascot costume throughout the agreed hours, engaged with conference visitors at the booth and outside the venue (accompanied by our staff at all times), and submitted photographic and video evidence from each day confirming their presence in costume on-site.
bounties.evidenceCriteria: There will be staff to assist on-site, but a photo and video evidence is appreciated. Evidence must be submitted at the end of each day.

applicationDetails.label: A short video to introduce yourself, age, height, where you're from and if you have the ability to travel to Brighton.

bounties.title: AI Model Evaluation Collaborator (US/Canada)
bounties.description:
We are looking for 1-2 reliable and detail-oriented individuals based in the US or Canada to collaborate on an ongoing AI model evaluation project.

**What You'll Be Doing:**
- Evaluating AI model outputs for quality, accuracy, relevance, and coherence
- Testing prompts and reviewing model responses
- Identifying errors, inconsistencies, or biases in AI-generated content
- Providing structured written feedback and ratings on model performance
- Collaborating closely with the project lead on an ongoing basis

**Who We're Looking For:**
- Based in the US or Canada
- Familiar with AI/ML concepts and language models
- Strong attention to detail and analytical thinking
- Good written communication skills in English
- Reliable, self-motivated, and able to work independently

This is a remote, ongoing collaboration. Hours are flexible and will be discussed with the selected candidate(s).
requirements: Must be based in the US or Canada
Familiarity with AI/ML concepts and large language models
Strong analytical and critical thinking skills
Excellent written English communication
Reliable and self-motivated
Available for ongoing collaboration
bounties.completionCriteria: Worker submits structured evaluation reports covering assigned AI model outputs, including ratings, written feedback, and flagged issues. Reports must be detailed, clearly written, and delivered on the agreed schedule.
bounties.evidenceCriteria: Submit a written evaluation report (or a link to a shared document) covering the assigned model outputs. Each report must include: ratings per output, written justification for each rating, and any flagged errors or concerns. At least one report must be submitted per agreed work session.

applicationDetails.label: Briefly describe your experience with AI/ML or language model evaluation.
applicationDetails.placeholder: e.g. I have tested GPT-4 outputs for a research project, rated responses for accuracy and bias...

applicationDetails.label: Are you based in the US or Canada? Please specify your country and state/province.

bounties.title: Dialogue editor: read all the lines in a small cozy game and flag what sounds stiff (about 4 hours, native English)
bounties.description:
Kal's Valley is a small, gentle walking game in a web browser: you help a valley of neighbours get their solar drones flying again. It has about 720 lines of dialogue (around 8,000 words) across 17 characters.

We want one careful reader to go through every line on a review web page we've built and tell us which lines sound stiff, generic, written rather than spoken, out of character, or too much like another character. For those, mark "flag" with a short reason, or "suggest" and write the line the way you'd have it, keeping that character's voice.

The page groups lines by character, shows each conversation together with who's speaking to whom, and has a short note on each character (who they are, how they talk). You mark each line fine / flag / suggest. Your answers save as you go, so you can do it in several sittings.

Things that are on purpose (please don't flag): all game text is lowercase; the valley is vegetarian; words from other languages (bà nội, peddatata, odi, teta, abuela...) are deliberate.

At the end you fill in three short notes: which characters sound too alike, the three biggest problems with the writing, and anything else.

We care about honest, specific notes far more than speed. A line you flag with a clear reason is worth more than ten lines marked fine.

Writing sample (in your application): rewrite this line so it sounds like a tired gardener actually said it: "the soil remembers every season we have given it."
requirements: Native or near-native English, with a good ear for how people actually talk
Comfortable reading on a laptop or desktop browser
About 4 hours, can be split over a day or two
bounties.completionCriteria: Every line on the review page answered (all ~720, about 8,000 words; the page shows your count), with a reason on each flag and a rewritten line on each suggestion, and the three overall notes filled in. Then press "done" on the page.
bounties.evidenceCriteria: Text: the line "you covered N lines (W words)" from the page, copied exactly, plus your three biggest problems in a few sentences. Photo: a screenshot of the page's count after pressing done.

applicationDetails.label: Your rewrite of the gardener line from the description
Any writing or editing you've done (fiction, games, scripts, subtitles)? A link or a sentence is fine.

bounties.title: 3D artist / animator: review a small game's characters and animations on a web page (45 min, portfolio required)
bounties.description:
we're a tiny team making a cozy, stylised 3d browser game (chunky, soft, storybook look). we'd like a trained eye on our characters and their animations before more people play it.

who: you model or animate characters (games, film, or personal work) and can show it. IN YOUR APPLICATION: a link to your portfolio/reel (artstation, youtube, website), and one line on what you mostly do.

what to do (about 45 minutes, phone or laptop - laptop is better):
1. we send you a private link to our review page. it shows each character from all sides and each animation as a looping video with front/side frame strips.
2. for each item: tap 'looks right', or 'not right' with a short note (tap on the picture to mark the spot). skip anything you're unsure about.
3. focus on what a player would notice: clipping, sliding feet, pops at the loop, stiff or floaty motion, odd proportions, silhouettes that don't read.
4. fill in the 'overall impressions' box: the 3 biggest problems and anything that's working well.
5. tap 'done' - it shows how many items you covered.

send back: the number of items you covered and your 3 biggest problems (also in the page). honest criticism is the point.
bounties.completionCriteria: At least 60 items reviewed on the private review page with notes on any 'not right', the overall-impressions box filled (3 biggest problems + what works), and the covered count reported.
